subject: Charlie Chaplin
hook: Charlie Chaplin's coffin was stolen two months after burial.
twist: The ransom was never paid; the only lasting change was that his grave was rebuilt under concrete.
mood: Muted sepia and slate-blue night palette, soft cut-paper/gouache illustration with grain, Swiss alpine dusk and cornfield textures. Score: sparse pizzicato strings and muted piano, slow 70 bpm, a gently ironic waltz that thins to a single note at the end.
narration: Charlie Chaplin's coffin was stolen two months after burial. He died on Christmas Day, nineteen seventy-seven, and was buried in Corsier-sur-Vevey. On the second of March, nineteen seventy-eight, two men took the coffin from the grave. Weeks later, a caller demanded a ransom. Reports put it near six hundred thousand. His widow, Oona, refused to pay. Police tapped her phone and watched two hundred phone booths. In May, they arrested two refugee mechanics, one Polish, one Bulgarian. They led police to the coffin, buried in a cornfield near Lake Geneva. The family reburied him under concrete. The leader got four and a half years. The ransom was never paid. The only thing the crime changed was his grave. Would you have paid the ransom?

Charlie Chaplin's coffin was stolen two months after burial. 🎩

Charlie Chaplin died on Christmas Day 1977 and was buried at Corsier-sur-Vevey, Switzerland. On 2 March 1978 his coffin was taken from the grave.

A caller demanded a ransom, reported as about 600,000 (accounts differ on dollars or Swiss francs). His widow Oona refused to pay. Police tapped the phone and watched 200 phone booths.

In May they arrested two refugee mechanics, one Polish, one Bulgarian. The coffin was found buried in a cornfield near Lake Geneva. The family reburied him under concrete. The leader got four and a half years.

The ransom was never paid. The only thing the crime changed was his grave.
